answer_1.quote: We propose an algorithm for One-to-N Unsupervised Sequence transduction (ONUS) that learns to map from the distribution of hard questions to that of many simple questions... Our approach generates sub‑questions (decompositions) which are then answered by a single‑hop QA model.

answer_2.quote: We compute the likelihood of decompositions using the pretrained GPT‑2 language model ... We also measure how abstractive decompositions are by computing (i) the token Levenshtein distance between the multihop question and its generated decomposition and (ii) the ratio between the length of the decomposition and the length of the multihop question ... To stop ONUS training, we use an unsupervised stopping criterion ... we measure BLEU between q and the model‑generated question q for d, similar to round‑trip BLEU.
